Case: Patient D is a 66-year-old White man who presents with 3 months of low-back pain. The pain is primarily axial and is exacerbated by bending, twisting and heavy lifting. On physical exam, his lumbar spine is tender to palpation, but he has no focal neurologic deficits. On further questioning, he reveals that he has had intermittent fevers and night sweats ever since he was hospitalized for a kidney infection 5 months ago.
